_howto: One object per rule. Keep each rule to one idea. Ids use CATEGORY-NN so the model can cite them. A parent name (Alert) covers its parts (AlertTitle, AlertDescription). If a rule lists components and message types, both must match.

rules.rule: Keep all text as action-oriented unless supplemental information is required to help the user move to the next step or to provide reassurance.
rules.dont: This field is for your SSN.

rules.do: Clear browsing data and try again
rules.dont: Request header fields are too large.

rules.rule: Don't include punctuation on headings, toasts, badges, buttons.
Use sentence case for buttons, labels, and headings.

rules.do: We'll use your email for application reviews.
rules.dont: We will use your email for application reviews.

rules.rule: Don't include words that describe the page type, like Dashboard, Page, or Screen. Name the page by its content.
Label buttons with the action and keep it short. Use just the verb when the screen makes the object clear, like Save, Submit, or Run.
Use sentences for all secondary text with punctuation.
rules.do: Enter 8 or more characters. Include a number.
rules.dont: Enter 8 or more characters include a number

rules.rule: Add supplemental information only when it's important to reassure the user about sensitive information or what's going to happen next. If the original doesn't include this information, flag that it's missing instead of writing it.
rules.do: Enter your SSN. Your data won't be stored. /Flag: Consider saying how SSN data is used
rules.dont: Enter your SSN your data won't be stored

rules.rule: Don't use punctuation for descriptions that describe the state of the field, like required and optional. This overrides DESCRIPTIONS-01.
Keep toast messages concise with 5 words or fewer.
Error toast messages should be converted to Alerts with AlertTitle and AlertDescription.
rules.do: AlertTitle: Upload files with type PNG, JPEG, or PDF

rules.rule: Warning dialog titles should be in the form of a question, action followed by the object. Question marks are allowed.
rules.dont: You're discarding your changes, confirm to continue.

rules.rule: Start with a verb to be action-oriented on what the user can do to solve the error.
rules.do: Enter a different email. This email is already in use.
rules.dont: Invalid input! You entered a duplicate email.

rules.rule: Don't blame the user in error scenarios. Say what happened, not what the user did wrong. Mentioning the user's own things isn't blame: 'Your card was declined' is fine; 'You entered the wrong card number' isn't.
rules.do: Upload a file type of PNG, JPEG, or PDF
rules.dont: You entered the wrong file type.

rules.rule: If the user isn't allowed to solve the issue, start with the word Couldn't followed by the incomplete action for the primary text. For the secondary text, tell the user to please contact a system administrator for help, if that is what applies. This overrides ERR-01
rules.do: Title: Couldn't access that page / Description: Please contact your system administrator for permissions.
rules.dont: Invalid input! You can't get in.

rules.rule: Start progress messages with the gerund form of the action verb.
Empty state titles should start with an action verb encouraging users to do something to fill the empty state.
Focus on the purpose of the empty state without negative wording to the user.
rules.do: Create or import a project to get started.
rules.dont: You haven't created any projects yet.
